title: PCA 15 9 coconut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: PCA 15 9 coconut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: PCA 15 9 coconut is a coconut variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: PCA 15 9 is a registered coconut variety, also sold or known as Tacunan Dwarf x Tagnanan Tall or TACD x TAGT. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2000 as NSIC 2000 Co 20. Its record notes 2.11 tonnes of copra per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

Its average yield of 2.11 t copra/ha beats the average of its group, 1.85. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit coconut fields most often: [coconut bud rot](/diseases/coconut-bud-rot), [coconut cadang cadang](/diseases/cadang-cadang), [coconut leaf beetle (Brontispa)](/pests/coconut-leaf-beetle), [coconut rhinoceros beetle](/pests/coconut-rhinoceros-beetle), [coconut scale insect (cocolisap)](/pests/cocolisap). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of PCA 15 9 weighs about 1,434.7 + 184.7 g grams, and its shape is round (polar and equatorial). The edible part is 59.6 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is 12, bearing biennial. Each palm gave about 67 nuts a year in the records, with 303 grams of copra per nut.

**Fruit:** Big nuts about 1.4 kg, about 303 g copra per nut.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: produced at the Bohol seed garden and planted in Davao Oriental to replace typhoon hit palms, on the VCO list. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant PCA 15 9 coconut

Talls live long and stand typhoons, dwarfs bear early and are easy to harvest, and hybrids between the two give the most copra. Pick by use: copra, buko, or both. Get seednuts from a PCA accredited source. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for tree crops](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Tacunan Dwarf x Tagnanan Tall the same as PCA 15 9?
items.a: Yes. Tacunan Dwarf x Tagnanan Tall is another name for PCA 15 9, registered as NSIC 2000 Co 20. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows 2.11 tonnes of copra per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of PCA 15 9?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
